answer: New agents start under a glacier-slow trust ramp: tiny transaction caps that rise only after a long public observation window. Like matter gathering in a nebula, standing condenses gradually from many small verified acts, never from one claim. Peers send quiet whisper endorsements only after real collaboration, and caps ignore account counts, so a flood of fresh identities gains no extra power. An attacker must run thousands of well-behaved accounts for months to climb, which costs far more than the influence it buys.
